info.name: TetraFi API
info.description: Generated from the TetraFi integrator specification. Set baseUrl, apiKey and signingSecret in your local collection variables. Start with GET /api/v1/assets. Replace angle-bracket placeholders with real values before sending other requests; review each write rather than running the entire collection. Never share populated credentials.

exec: // Never retain headers from an earlier signed send when signing is turned off.
// Resolve variables ONCE, including dynamic variables, before hashing and sending.
if (!parts) throw new Error('Set baseUrl to an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL');
// Encode explicitly and disable subsequent transport encoding, so the signed
// target is exactly what is sent. Keep already percent-encoded bytes unchanged.
if (pm.request.body.mode !== 'raw') throw new Error('Signing supports raw request bodies only');
// JSON comments are not valid API input and Postman would strip them AFTER
// signing. Refuse them rather than signing bytes different from the wire.
if (!/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(secret)) throw new Error('signingSecret must contain 64 hexadecimal characters');
// A write needs a nonce accepted once per key: a new random UUID on every send.
if (nonce !== null && !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/.test(nonce)) throw new Error('Could not generate an X-Nonce');
const canonical = [timestamp, ...(nonce === null ? [] : [nonce]), method, pathWithQuery, digest].join('\n');
if (nonce !== null) pm.request.headers.upsert({ key: 'X-Nonce', value: nonce });

request.description:
List tradable assets

Lists the assets your workspace can trade, with their variants and networks. Call it first, and take the asset ids and networks for prices and quotes from it.

query.description: Assets per page, 1 to 200. May change between pages; omit it to keep the cursor's page size.

The previous page's `nextCursor`: the next page lists the Assets after the last one the
previous page listed, in Asset id order, as listed now. It stays valid while the listing
changes (an Asset added or removed between pages is listed or not by where it falls); a
cursor issued for another workspace, or for other filters (`venueId`, `venueCode`, `network`,
`address`, compared after trimming), answers 409 `CURSOR_STALE`: send the filters the first
page was asked with, or start again without a cursor.
`registry`: the registry snapshot the listing was built from, in `included.registry`.

Only assets a venue offers this workspace, on-chain venues included: its venue id (`valr`,
every entry of it) or one venue entry (`valr-orderbook`, that entry only). With `venueCode`,
only the asset that venue's code is (`USC` at `b2c2` is USDC), and only when the instance the
code names, its variant included, is offered at that same venue or entry (`USDT0` is USDT
variant USDT0 at `valr-orderbook`, nothing at `valr-rfq`). Every filter narrows the listing;
an empty value answers 400 `ASSET_FILTER_BLANK` with `details.field` naming the filter.

A venue's own code for an asset; needs `venueId` (otherwise 400 `ASSET_FILTER_INCOMPLETE`
with `details.field` `venueCode`).

Only assets with a deployment on this CAIP-2 network (`eip155:1`). With `address`, only the
asset deployed at that address there.

A token address on `network`, in that chain's own form (EVM hex, Solana base58, Tron
base58check or hex; a form of another chain family matches nothing); needs `network` (otherwise 400 `ASSET_FILTER_INCOMPLETE` with `details.field`
`address`). A token the registry does not list matches nothing, whatever it
calls itself.

header.description: Makes a retry safe. Required for every caller, member session or API key (a missing key answers 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED). 1 to 255 bytes, unique per order you mean to place; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same principal in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer and never places a second order. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; another principal's key answers 403 IDEMPOTENCY_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it before any other check (an expired quote or price included), answers what the first request answered, and answers 409 ORDER_IN_PROGRESS (with Retry-After) if it is still running after 30 seconds. A retry after a first request that may have placed an order (it stopped without an answer, or was refused with `details.placementEffect` `uncertain`) answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN before any other check, with no Retry-After: retrying that key can never settle it, so read the orders back (GET /api/v1/orders, details.readTarget) and use a new key only once the order is not there. One `uncertain` refusal releases its key: a source transaction's registration refused while its receipt is pending or unreadable; send the same request again once the transaction is readable (the quote still places at most one order). A refusal marked `noOrder` is not stored: fix the request and send it again with the same key or a new one.
Signed-in sessions whose member turned on the check for orders: a step-up proof for purpose `order_placement` bound to this quote. Ignored for API keys.

`respond-async` (RFC 7240): answer once the order is claimed rather than at the venue's outcome. A venue order then answers 202 with the claimed order (`working`), `Location` naming it and `Preference-Applied: respond-async`; read the order at its `statusUrl` (or follow its `order.updated` events) until `terminal` is `true`. An order that can only answer at its outcome answers as without the preference, with no `Preference-Applied`. Other preferences are ignored. Every refusal before the claim still answers this request. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key answers the same order as it reads now, with or without the preference.

header.description: Makes a retry safe; optional. 1 to 255 bytes; a UUID is a good choice. A retry with the same key and the same body, from the same credential's owner in the same workspace within 24 hours, returns the first answer (header Idempotent-Replayed: true; its quotes may have expired since) and asks no venue again. The same key with a different body answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a retry while the first is still running waits for its answer. Refusals are not stored. Not accepted with Accept: text/event-stream (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID): a streamed answer cannot be replayed.

request.description:
One inventory account with every position and its breakdown

The account as the list shows it, under the same admission (a member without `view_wallets` reads only wallets whose resource policy permits their balances). A missing or hidden account is `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`. A retired organisation wallet, which the list leaves out, still reads here with `retiredAt`, read-only. Registered external wallets with detail permission carry `ownership.status`: `proven`, `pending`, `notProven`, `noLongerHolds` or `unknown`, plus retained proof time, prover and signature method. A departed prover makes the proof no longer hold; failed evidence or membership reads are unknown. Organisation wallets and custody accounts carry no ownership field. A wallet originally created by a venue whitelist import carries `whitelistImport {venue, venueConnectionId, at}` from that import's registration; manual wallets carry none. Original hidden policies remain hidden. Provider observations are read-only facts, never signing authority. Privy owner sessions cannot be observed server-side; Turnkey has no per-wallet login session. No provider call is made. `include=controls` adds the account's control register as `included.controls[<accountId>]` (never inline as `controls`), projected exactly as its row in the list projects it; it is the only relation one account takes.

request.description:
List the workspace's money movements

Signed-in sessions, and API keys (unsigned) holding treasury_read or settlements_read. Every money movement of the workspace as one Movement list, newest first by occurredAt (sort=-occurredAt, the default) or oldest first (sort=occurredAt, which needs from: the window is read whole and refused past 1,000 movements): treasury transfers, payouts and agent payments, venue deposits and withdrawals, LP bank payouts and deposits, deferred deposits, withdrawals and claims, and venue accounts' settlement transfers. Each source is read through its own list route as the caller and keeps that route's permission, visibility and API-key scope rules: treasury kinds need View wallets (treasury_read for a key), venue kinds View orders and View wallets in a signed-in session, LP bank kinds an LP workspace with View settlements, deferred kinds the workspace's settlement read, and settlement transfers View settlements (settlements_read for a key), read per venue account from their settlement owner (they have no other read): the accountId values, else every venue account the caller's account list names (more than 100 is 400 asking for accountId). A source the caller cannot read is left out, never widened; when every source refuses, or the one kind named refuses, the answer is that refusal. Any other failed source read refuses the page with 503 MOVEMENTS_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE naming the source; narrow kind to read the rest. data is the source's own record. Filters (comma = any of): kind, direction, accountId, asset, network (CAIP-2), status, tradeId (the taker's trade a venue deposit declaration or withdrawal funds), subjectId (the source record's own id), agentId (agent payments only), deskId, ownerUserId and directUserId (one value each, deferred kinds only, passed to the deferred read as its own scope), windowId (one settlement window, settlement transfers only), and the half-open window from/to over occurredAt. The first page pins the window's end, so later pages read the same selection; a cursor is bound to the sort and every filter. fields=a,b returns only those row fields (id, kind, status, direction and occurredAt always kept). include=account,trade adds each row's account by accountId and trade by tradeId, as their own GETs answer the caller, or null with their refusal. Counts and per-asset sums are GET …/movements:aggregate.

-occurredAt (newest first, the default) or occurredAt (oldest first: needs from; the window is read whole, at most 1,000 movements)

request.description:
Read one money movement

Signed-in sessions, and API keys (unsigned) holding treasury_read or settlements_read. One movement by its id (kind:sourceId, as the list returns it), exactly as the list returns its row: the source is read through its own list route as the caller, with that route's permission and visibility rules, and the row is projected the same way. A source that refuses the caller answers with its own refusal; a movement that does not exist, belongs to another workspace or is hidden from the caller is 404 MOVEMENT_NOT_FOUND. A movement older than the read reaches (20 owner pages of its source) is 503 MOVEMENTS_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, never 404.

trade matches its execution type's venue) or an LP workspace UUID (orders only), the client workspace (umbrella) or the
